proposed_widenings.name: passive (ClassFeatureMechanics family)
proposed_widenings.justification: Body and Mind is a permanent, passive character-progression effect that grants a one-time ability score increase at level 20. It has no activation cost, no use-count resource, and no reset cadence — all three fields required by the only existing family ('activation'). Forcing it into 'activation' would be dishonest: there is nothing to activate, nothing to count, nothing to reset. A 'passive' family is needed for features whose effect is a durable state change applied at level acquisition.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

proposed_widenings.name: modify_ability_score
proposed_widenings.justification: The sole mechanical content of this feature is a permanent increase to two ability scores (Dexterity and Wisdom, +4, capped at 25). No existing ClassFeatureEffect covers this: 'grant_extra_action' is action-economy, 'heal_hp' is HP restoration. The v4 taxonomy notes 'modify_ability_score as a runtime effect versus as pre-runtime character state (currently treated as out-of-scope)' but Body and Mind and comparable L20 capstone features (Barbarian Primal Champion: Str/Con +4) apply at character creation/progression time — the engine must track the modified score for downstream computations. This forces 'modify_ability_score' into the atom inventory.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

notes: Structural widening on two axes: (1) ClassFeatureMechanics has no 'passive' family — every existing family assumes activation with use-count and reset cadence, none of which apply to a permanent capstone stat boost; (2) no effect atom covers permanent ability score modification. Both gaps are closely related: the atom is only needed because the family is also missing. Comparable unit: Barbarian Primal Champion (Str+4, Con+4). The taxonomy already flags modify_ability_score as a known weak spot.
